skill.name: using-superpowers
skill.description: Establishes a startup workflow for discovering, announcing, and following relevant skills before beginning tasks.
skill.summary: Guides agents to use relevant skills consistently before starting work.
skill.author: DYAI2025

security_audit.summary: The static system reconnaissance finding is a false positive because the referenced text only explains how to follow skill workflows. The archive was manually reviewed and contains only SKILL.md, with no additional executable or hidden content found.

static_findings.snippet: **Many skills contain rigid rules (TDD, debugging, verification).** Follow them exactly. Don't adapt

finding_verdicts.reason: The flagged line describes following skill workflow rules, not probing the host, enumerating systems, or collecting environment details. No reconnaissance intent or instructions were found in SKILL.md.
Manual archive review showed SKILL.zip contains only SKILL.md, which was already reviewed as the sole skill source file. No additional binary payload or hidden executable content was found.

low_findings.title: Unscanned file (binary) — manual review required
low_findings.confidence_reasoning: Force-confirmed metadata/low static finding; AI false-positive verdict rejected.

content.value_statement: Agents can miss important workflows when they start tasks too quickly. This skill makes skill discovery, announcement, and checklist tracking part of every task startup.
actual_capabilities: Requires agents to check for relevant skills before beginning a task.
Instructs agents to announce skill usage to the user before applying it.
Directs agents to read the current skill instructions instead of relying on memory.
Requires TodoWrite tracking when a selected skill includes a checklist.
Explains why process workflows still matter for simple or specific tasks.
limitations: Does not implement any automation or tool calls by itself.
Depends on the agent having access to a separate skill system.
Does not decide which domain-specific skill is best for a task.
Can add process overhead for very small one-step requests.

use_cases.title: Standardize agent task startup
use_cases.description: Use this to make every task begin with a check for relevant reusable workflows.
use_cases.target_user: Engineering teams using multiple AI skills

use_cases.title: Reduce skipped checklist steps
use_cases.description: Use this to require visible task tracking when a skill includes a checklist.

use_cases.title: Improve process transparency
use_cases.description: Use this to make agents announce which skill they are applying and why.
use_cases.target_user: Reviewers and managers supervising AI-assisted work

prompt_templates.title: Start with available skills
prompt_templates.prompt: Before starting this task, check whether a relevant skill exists and tell me which one you will use.

prompt_templates.title: Use the matching workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the best matching skill for this request, read its current instructions, and follow its workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Track checklist items visibly
prompt_templates.prompt: If the skill you select has a checklist, create separate todos for each checklist item before doing the work.

prompt_templates.title: Audit process compliance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this task plan and identify whether the agent selected, announced, and followed the relevant skills correctly.

output_examples.input: Fix this bug and use the right workflow.
output_examples.output: The agent identifies a debugging skill, announces its use, reads the skill, and follows the required steps before editing code.

output_examples.input: Implement this feature with a skill checklist.
output_examples.output: The agent creates one visible todo for each checklist item, completes them in order, and does not mark items done early.

output_examples.input: Check whether the process was followed.
output_examples.output: The agent reports whether skill discovery, announcement, reading, and checklist tracking happened as required.

best_practices: Use this skill at the start of a task, before implementation choices are made.
Read the selected skill every time because skill instructions may change.
Create separate checklist todos when a skill requires checklist tracking.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on memory of a skill instead of reading the current version.
Do not skip workflow steps because the task appears simple.
Do not combine multiple checklist requirements into one vague todo.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It tells an agent to find, announce, read, and follow relevant skills before starting work.

faq.question: Does it execute commands or access files?
faq.answer: No. It is instructional workflow guidance and does not include scripts or command execution.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it at the beginning of a conversation or task where other skills may apply.

faq.question: Why require an announcement?
faq.answer: The announcement makes the agent process visible and lets the user correct the chosen workflow early.

faq.question: Why are todos required for checklists?
faq.answer: Visible todos reduce the chance that checklist steps are skipped or marked complete too early.

faq.question: Can this replace domain-specific skills?
faq.answer: No. It helps select and follow other skills, but it does not provide domain-specific implementation guidance.
